transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:02
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortega - Redwood | Priya Nair, Carlos Ruiz, Dana Li, Evan Brooks - Greystone
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/console-forensics.pdf, security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf, sample replay sheet: https://redwood.ai/replays/greystone-sample.xlsx

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focusing on tracing + request replay, KV-cache mis-hit analysis, and how SLOs tie into fallback routing. Customer interested in doing a pilot to replay an anonymized production trace on a Dedicated pool.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh really appreciate you carving time. quick intros — im Maya, AE — Liam is our systems SE — we'll do a short walkthrough of the request path features then open for questions.
[00:32] Priya: thanks, maya. were excited — we run a mix of latency-sensitive inference for risk scoring and some batch jobs, goal is to understand how we can debug p95 spikes and correlate with downstream services.
[01:05] Carlos: yes and weve seen sporadic 99th percentile blips at 10pm PT the past month. wondering if its kv cache thrashing or model cold starts.
[01:30] Liam: good, thats exactly what the console playthrough targets. quick note, i may jumble some names, the transcript may have mis-heard bits.
[01:45] Maya: first demo slide — request timeline view. this stitches the trace, token-level latency, and any external calls. so you can see when a request waited on the KV-cache read vs when the model compute kicked off.
[02:20] [screen share starts] Liam: ok starting the console — top left timeline shows p50/p95 and request count. you can click an individual request and get a waterfall, the waterfall has annotations for cache hits, kv reads, and fallback paths.
[03:10] Dana: are the KV-cache hits stored per customer or per-route? we've got multi-tenant rules so want to ensure isolation.
[03:28] Liam: isolation is per deployment; for Hosted we have logical namespaces, for Dedicated you can bind caches to GPU pools. in private/on-prem you control the cache instance.
[03:50] Carlos: what's the retention for request logs? we have compliance constraints.
[04:05] Maya: standard is 30 days for request-level payloads but we have enterprise retention add-ons; also payloads can be redacted at ingestion and you can integrate with your KMS so PII is encrypted at rest.
[04:30] Priya: do you have SOC2 and key management diagrams?
[04:40] Maya: yes sending after the call — SOC2, network layout screenshots, HSM/KMS notes — link in the follow-up.
[04:52] Liam: back to the console — here's a noisy window where p95 spikes. you can filter to requests that used a specific model variant. note the vertical band, click into it.
[05:20] [05:20] Liam: opening a single request. at the top: request metadata, tags, route config used. timeline shows 73ms pre-processing, 310ms model compute, 14ms post-processing. under 'cache' it shows 'miss' and then a fallback to a smaller quantized model.
[06:05] Priya: ok that fallback detail is great. how are fallbacks configured — is it automatic? can we tune thresholds?
[06:18] Liam: yes, policies are config-driven. you can set latency thresholds, error-rate thresholds, or queue depth. when a threshold is hit, routing policy will send to a cheaper/quantized variant or failover cluster. it's all visible in the request trace, plus we surface which policy triggered the fallback.
[06:45] Evan: can we see the token-level timing? e.g., where KV cache saved time inside the autoregressive loop?
[06:55] Liam: yep, token breakdown is shown if you have KV-cache enabled. this is where we show cache warm/hits as microsecond-level deltas — sometimes the transcription may show micro-deltas as ms, but the console shows more precision.
[07:30] [07:30] Priya: our team uses an internal correlator ID, can we daisy-chain that through traces?
[07:42] Liam: absolutely — you can map any customer-side headers to trace keys; we stitch via the correlator. we also ingest application-level logs and match by request id so you can see app logs inline.
[08:05] Carlos: what's the overhead of enabling the trace and token timing? we worry about additional latency.
[08:15] Liam: sampling can mitigate overhead — default is sampled at 1% for high-volume routes; for pilot we usually do 100% for the replay window but on production you'd sample. the runtime does a lightweight profiler that adds minimal overhead; measurement error can be in the low single-digit percent.
[08:50] [08:50] Liam: switching to replay — this is the 'request replay' surface. you upload a sanitized trace or point the console at a stored trace, choose destination (Hosted/Dedicated/private), set model variant, and run. you get a side-by-side: original output vs replayed output and timing differences.
[09:30] Dana: can the replay simulate peak concurrency? we want to repro contention with KV-cache under load.
[09:42] Liam: yes, you can set concurrency and RPS in the replay run. we run those jobs on isolated test pools; for Dedicated pilots we can spin a temporary burst pool to mimic prod capacity.
[10:05] Priya: curious about quantization and perf — if we replay on a quantized variant, will the token timings be comparable?
[10:20] Liam: they will differ, but the console highlights where quantization changed compute time vs where cache behavior is unchanged. we show delta columns and a regression flag if output quality deviates beyond thresholds.
[10:55] [10:55] Carlos: about SLOs — can we map request failures to SLO burn? e.g., if a fallback trips, does that increment the error budget?
[11:08] Liam: yes, SLO rules can be defined per-route. fallbacks that preserve successful responses don't necessarily count as errors, but if you configure 'strict' mode then any non-primary model counts as an error. we surface SLO burn rate with links from the trace to the SLO dashboard.
[11:40] Maya: sounds like a question on policy tradeoffs — cost vs fidelity — that we can model in the spreadsheet i'll send.
[11:55] [11:55] Evan: we also have encryption-at-rest rules and a customer-managed KMS requirement for some markets. how does Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM?
[12:07] Maya: for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS using KMS proxies; keys can be stored in your HSM and we never export plaintext. we have a short integration guide i'll attach.
[12:30] [12:30] Liam: walking through an error case — here's a request that timed out at the load-balancer. timeline shows an initial spike in CPU on the model pod and then a queue buildup. the console surfaces the node metrics and the autoscaler events.
[13:05] Priya: can we get alerting on autoscaler thrash? we need alpha alerts before customers experience latency.
[13:15] Liam: yes alerting hooks are built into the console; you can emit alerts to PagerDuty/Slack and also to an internal webhook where you can run automated mitigation like scale-up.
[13:40] [13:40] Carlos: tell me about multi-region fallbacks and cold starts — we have global users.
[13:52] Liam: smart routing can failover to a nearby region or to a lower-cost region; cold-starts are mitigated with warm pools and pre-warming heuristics. the trace will show the region switch and the reasons it triggered.
[14:25] Priya: how do you handle private deployments with customer network policies? we need our inference to not egress anything.
[14:35] Maya: Private option supports air-gapped installs and a customer-managed control plane. we ship an on-prem package and all telemetry can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[14:52] [14:52] Evan: do you keep raw request payloads in logs by default?
[15:00] Liam: defaults to redacted; you can opt-in to store plaintext for a limited retention window. again enterprise retention + redaction rules can be tuned.
[15:22] [15:22] Maya: quick note on troubleshooting: our SE playbook includes a step-by-step to identify whether a p95 spike is compute, cache, or routing. we'll share that runbook.
[15:40] [15:40] Priya: ok let's try a live micro-replay. we'll load a small scrubbed trace we prepared.
[15:50] Liam: great, upload it now and i'll kick off a replay. bear with me while the upload finishes.
[16:30] [16:30] Liam: upload complete, configuring target — we'll run it against a Dedicated trial pool using quantized-1 and primary-1 models for comparison. starting replay now.
[17:05] [17:05] Liam: replay finished. side-by-side shows a couple of requests where the replay p95 is 1.8x original. click the request id.
[17:30] [17:30] Liam: this one shows a cache miss in replay but original had a warm cache at time-of-day. looks like your production cache TTL is short, causing thrash under replay concurrency.
[17:50] Priya: is TTL configurable per-route?
[17:58] Liam: yes per-route and per-key-type. you can also enable async-prefetch for common prefixes which avoids blocking on cache fills.
[18:20] Carlos: can we surface which keys are cold? we need to run a warm-up job.
[18:30] Liam: console shows cold-key heatmap; we also export a key-summary CSV.
[18:50] [18:50] Dana: noticed a few model outputs diverged in content when we used quantized variant. is there an eval metric for semantic similarity?
[19:02] Liam: yes we compute embedding cosine similarity and BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics per-replay; we flag regressions and allow you to set accept/reject thresholds.
[19:30] Priya: what's the process to move from pilot to Dedicated? timeline-wise?
[19:42] Maya: usually a 2-4 week pilot to run replays and perf tests, then a procurement + capacity reservation — for Dedicated we'd propose a small initial pool for 3 months then scale.
[20:05] Evan: pricing sensitivity — if we use fallbacks frequently, how does billing look? is it per-token primary only or includes fallback compute?
[20:18] Maya: billing records the actual compute used per request path; if a request falls back to a different model we bill for the model that served tokens. the spreadsheet i'll send lays out typical unit economics.
[20:45] [20:45] Carlos: any enterprise customers running a similar footprint?
[20:55] Maya: yes, a couple of fintechs are similar — we can share anonymized case studies.
[21:10] [21:10] Priya: one last question — does replay preserve exact randomness seeds so outputs deterministic?
[21:20] Liam: we can replay with fixed seeds to get deterministic output for debugging, or with live randomness to mimic production. deterministic replay is default for deep-diffing.
[21:42] [21:42] Maya: ok great. recap and next steps — Maya to send SOC2, pricing + spreadsheet; Liam to send replay runbook and the sample curl scripts; Priya to share scrubbed trace by 1/18. schedule pilot kickoff for next week?
[22:05] Priya: yes, let's tentatively book 1/19 for the pilot kickoff.
[22:15] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributed speaker lines, some proper nouns garbled (e.g., 'quantized-1' transcribed as 'quantized one'), filler words preserved.

End of meeting.
